title: Palworld Pal Spheres and Catching Guide | Every Sphere Tier and Catch Tips | Palworld Guide
description: How Pal Spheres work in Palworld: the six main tiers from Pal Sphere to Legendary Sphere, their unlock levels, crafting materials and the habits that raise your catch rate.

sections.heading: Why spheres matter
sections.script: Everything in Palworld starts with a throw. Every Pal on your team, every worker in your base and every mount you ride was caught with a Pal Sphere. In this guide we go through the sphere tiers, the levels where each one unlocks, what you need to craft them, and the habits that make your catches land far more often. The unlock levels in this video match several current guides and the community wiki. Where a source disagrees, I will say roughly, so you are never misled. If you have ever watched a sphere bounce off a Pal you really wanted, this one is for you. Grab your spheres, trainer, and let's start with the basics.

sections.heading: The six main tiers
sections.script: There are six main tiers that most players use. The basic Pal Sphere comes first, and it unlocks very early, around level two. After that you get the Mega Sphere at level fourteen, the Giga Sphere at level twenty, the Hyper Sphere at level twenty seven, the Ultra Sphere at level thirty five and the Legendary Sphere at level forty four. Sources agree on these numbers, which makes them easy to remember. Each tier has a higher capture power than the one before it. Exact capture power numbers differ between guides, so I will not quote them. What matters is the direction: every step up gives you a better chance on a tougher Pal. You also pay technology points to unlock each tier in the technology menu.

sections.heading: Crafting the early spheres
sections.script: The basic Pal Sphere is cheap. It needs one Paldium Fragment, three wood and three stone, and you can craft it at the Primitive Workbench. The Mega Sphere adds an ingot and a few more wood and stone, and the Giga Sphere doubles the Paldium Fragments and the ingots. Guides say both are made at a Sphere Workbench. A simple habit saves you many trips: before you leave your base, craft a good stack of basic spheres. One guide suggests about ten as a starting point. Paldium Fragments appear in every recipe, so keep a steady supply, because running out of them is the most common reason players run out of spheres. A missed throw wastes the sphere, so stock up generously.

sections.heading: Crafting the late spheres
sections.script: From the Hyper Sphere onward, the recipes get serious. Hyper uses three Paldium Fragments, three ingots, wood and cement. The Ultra Sphere asks for refined ingots, carbon fiber and cement. The Legendary Sphere is the most expensive of the six, with ten Paldium Fragments, Pal Metal Ingots, carbon fiber and cement. Guides say these later tiers are crafted on the Sphere Assembly Line upgrades instead of the basic workbench, so plan your base for them. Wooden spheres will not carry you forever. If you spend a little time automating your ingot and cement supply, you will never be stuck at the workbench when you find a rare Pal. Beyond the Legendary Sphere, guides mention even higher tiers for the late game, so check your technology menu as you level.

sections.heading: Match the sphere to the Pal
sections.script: The most important rule is simple: match the sphere to the Pal. The community wiki gives rough level bands. Basic spheres suit Pals up to about level thirteen, Mega spheres cover the teens, Giga spheres the twenties, Hyper spheres up to the mid thirties, Ultra spheres up to the low forties, and Legendary spheres from level forty four. A sphere that is too weak will simply fail against a high level Pal. A sphere that is too strong is a waste on a low level Pal, since guides advise saving your best spheres for tough or valuable targets. Think of it as a ladder. Climb it as you level, and always carry the tier that suits the Pals of your current area.

sections.heading: Weaken before you throw
sections.script: The biggest boost you control is the Pal's health. Multiple guides agree that lowering a Pal's health is the strongest way to raise your odds. Attack it, but do not knock it out, then throw when its health bar is low and the bar turns red. Choose a weak attack or a weaker Pal for this job, because a heavy hit can finish the target before you throw. Many guides also suggest putting a status effect on the target if you can, such as sleep or a burn, though results vary by Pal. Patience wins here. A careful approach with a few weak attacks catches more Pals than a rushed fight, and it saves you spheres in the long run.

sections.heading: Check the odds and aim for the back
sections.script: Palworld tells you your chance before you commit. Hold the throw button while aiming at the Pal, and the game shows the capture percentage. Do not throw at very low numbers. One guide author found that around sixty percent or higher worked well, while one hundred percent is ideal. Another trick is the back throw. Both the wiki and other guides say that throwing from behind a Pal gives a bonus, and one guide puts it at up to around twenty percent depending on the Pal. So circle the Pal, stay out of its sight when you can, and throw at its back. Combined with low health and the right tier, this turns a risky catch into a confident one.

sections.heading: Lifmunk Effigies
sections.script: There is also a permanent upgrade. Lifmunk Effigies are small statues you find around the world, and you can offer them at a Statue of Power. That raises your own capture power for every sphere you ever throw. The wiki and other guides advise collecting them and leveling this bonus as you explore. It does not feel exciting like a new weapon, yet it quietly improves every catch from now on. If you pass an effigy while exploring, pick it up. You will thank yourself later when you stand in front of a rare Pal with a single Legendary Sphere left in your bag, and the percentage on screen is a little higher than it would have been.

sections.heading: Alpha Pals and legendaries
sections.script: Alpha Pals and legendary Pals need extra care. Alpha Pals are giant versions that spawn in fixed places, and guides say they are harder to catch. The usual method is to bring their health into the red zone and then use your best spheres. One guide also says that butchering a captured boss gives extra loot, which is a nice reward for the effort. Legendary Pals work the same way: prepare, bring your strongest spheres, and weaken them carefully. Also match your level to the fight, use the element that the Pal is weak to, and dodge the big telegraphed attacks. Do not give up after one miss. Retreat, recover, and come back with a full stack.

sections.heading: Your catching checklist
sections.script: Let's put it all together. Carry a stack of the best spheres you can craft. Match the tier to the Pal's level. Weaken the target until its health is low, but do not knock it out. Hold the button to see the odds, and aim for the back when you can. Keep collecting Lifmunk Effigies to raise your capture power. Keep Paldium flowing into your base, because every recipe needs it. These habits will save you spheres and time, and they will help you fill your Palbox with the Pals you really want. Now tell me in the comments: which Pal took you the most spheres to catch, and how many did it cost you? If this guide helped, like the video and subscribe for more Palworld guides.
